on_unmapped_default: warn+record-unsupported (NEVER coerce a custom visual to a chart)
unknown_guidance: Unrecognized custom visual '{token}'. It is NOT in viz-kind.json or custom-visual.json and its name gives no filtering hint, so no Sigma kind was assumed — it is recorded as unsupported rather than silently rendered as a chart. To resolve: open the visual in Power BI, note what it BINDS (its fields) and what it DOES (filter / show a number / plot a series / list rows), then either add a row to refs/catalogs/custom-visual.json (match: a stable substring of '{token}') or hand-build the closest Sigma element. If it filters, a Sigma list or date-range control is almost always the right target.
heuristic_guidance: Unlisted custom visual '{token}' — its name matches the slicer/filter heuristic, so it is treated as a FILTER and emitted as a Sigma {kind} control targeting the page base element. This is deliberately conservative: a control the user can retarget is recoverable, whereas silently rendering a filter as a chart deletes the page's filter. Verify the binding, then add an explicit row to custom-visual.json for '{token}'.
description: Third-party / AppSource Power BI custom visuals -> Sigma element or control. A custom visual's `visualType` in the report Layout is the vendor's package id, so it is matched by CASE-INSENSITIVE REGEX on that token (`match`), first row wins, rather than by exact key. This catalog exists because the pipeline previously coerced every unrecognized visualType to a bar chart: on 4 real customer .pbix files that turned 21 third-party DATE-PICKER SLICERS into bar charts, silently removing the date filter from nearly every page. `role_class` control means the visual FILTERS and must become a Sigma control targeting the page's base element -- never a chart. `sigma_target` is the concrete Sigma control/element kind; `sigma` is the coarse builder token (rec['sigma_kind']). Vendor ids drift between releases, so patterns match the STABLE product-name substring, and lib/pbi_viz_kind.{rb,py} applies a generic slicer/filter/picker heuristic after this catalog so an unlisted filtering visual still lands as a control rather than a bogus chart.

rows.guidance: Third-party DATE-PICKER slicer (Powerviz / OrgStore and similar). Sigma HAS a native equivalent: a date-range control (controlType:date-range + mode:between). Emit that control bound to the visual's date column and target the page's base element -- do not render a chart. Its relative-date presets (Last 365 Days / YTD) map to Sigma date-range preset options.
rows.notes: Measured 21 instances across 3 of 4 customer reports (7 + 9 + 5), every one previously emitted as a bar chart. This single row is the highest-impact entry in the catalog.

rows.guidance: Chiclet Slicer = a categorical multi-select slicer rendered as buttons/tiles. Map to a Sigma list control (mode:include, selectionMode:multiple) targeting the page base element. The button styling has no Sigma equivalent and is a cosmetic-only difference.
rows.notes: One of the most common custom visuals in the wild.

rows.guidance: Hierarchy Slicer = an expandable multi-level slicer over 2+ hierarchy columns. Sigma has no single hierarchical control: emit ONE list control PER hierarchy level (parent -> child), each targeting the page base element, so the cascade still filters. Record as degraded (interaction simplified, no data lost).
rows.notes: Common with org / geography hierarchies -- exactly the org-hierarchy shape in customer report R1.

rows.guidance: Timeline Slicer = a horizontal date-range brush. Map to a Sigma date-range control (mode:between). Its granularity buttons (year/quarter/month/day) have no direct equivalent; the date-range control covers the filtering behaviour.
Free-text search slicer. Map to a Sigma text-input control with a Contains filter on the bound column, targeting the page base element.

Play Axis animates a report by stepping a field through its values. Sigma has no animation. Closest behaviour: emit a Sigma list control on that field so the user can step through values manually. Record as unsupported (the animation is lost) rather than approximating it as a chart.

Zebra BI tables/charts are IBCS variance reporting visuals. Map to a Sigma pivot table with explicit variance columns (actual, plan, delta, delta %) plus conditional formatting; a Zebra BI chart maps to a Sigma bar chart with a reference mark for plan. The IBCS notation itself (hatched variance bars) is cosmetic and not reproducible.
rows.notes: Data and numbers are fully recoverable; only the IBCS styling is lost.

rows.guidance: Inforiver is a writeback / planning matrix. Map the reporting half to a Sigma pivot table; if the visual is used for WRITEBACK, the Sigma equivalent is an input table (see the sigma-input-table-app skill) -- flag it for the user, since writeback changes the migration's scope.
rows.notes: Writeback usage is a scope decision, not a mechanical conversion -- always surface it.

rows.guidance: ZoomCharts Drill Down visuals are standard chart types with click-to-drill. Map to the matching Sigma chart kind (combo -> combo-chart, donut -> donut-chart, column/bar -> bar-chart) and wire Sigma drilldown on the hierarchy columns. Data preserved; the on-click zoom animation is not.

Third-party geospatial visual. Map to a Sigma region-map (admin regions) or a point/scatter map when the visual binds lat/long. Custom shapefiles, routes and flow lines have no Sigma equivalent -- record as degraded and list the bound geo fields. Synoptic Panel (custom SVG areas) has NO equivalent: report unsupported.
rows.notes: Measured 1 iconMapPro instance in customer report R1.

rows.guidance: Bullet chart = actual vs target with qualitative bands. Map to a Sigma bar chart with a reference mark for the target; the coloured bands map to conditional formatting.

Gantt visual. Sigma has no native Gantt: closest is a table with start/end/duration columns plus data bars on duration, or a horizontal bar chart per task. Record as degraded and keep all bound fields.

Specialist chart type with no currently published workbook-spec equivalent (sankey / word cloud / network / chord / sunburst / radar / tornado / box-whisker / violin, etc.). Two honest options, both recorded rather than faked: (1) build it as a Sigma custom plugin -- see the sigma-plugin-development skill; (2) substitute the nearest standard Sigma chart (sunburst/radar -> grouped bar; tornado -> diverging bar; box-whisker -> a reviewed quartile table/bar) and mark it approximated. Box-whisker remains an explicit gap until `box-chart` is published in workbook-as-code. Never emit a plain bar chart silently.
rows.notes: Grouped into one row because the guidance and the decision are identical for all of them. Keep box plots on this fallback even if another Sigma surface names box-chart; the workbook code representation does not publish it yet.

rows.guidance: Third-party KPI / card visual. Map to a Sigma KPI element (one per bound measure), with conditional formatting for the state colours and a reference mark for the target where one is bound.
Heatmap / calendar-heatmap. Map to a Sigma pivot table with a colour-scale conditional format on the measure -- this preserves both the values and the visual encoding.
